title: Book 3 — Thalia, Chapter 102
paragraphs: Others of the Indians are on the borders of the city of Caspatyros and the country of Pactyïke, dwelling to the north of the other Indians. Their manner of life is nearly the same as that of the Bactrians. These are the most warlike of the Indians, and it is they who make the expeditions for gold. For in the parts where they live the land is desert, on account of the sand; and in this desert and sandy tract ants are produced, smaller in size than dogs but larger than foxes. In fact some of them, caught here, are kept at the residence of the king of Persia. These ants build their dwellings underground and carry up the sand in the same manner as the ants in the land of the Hellenes, which they much resemble in form; and the sand they bring up contains gold. To obtain this sand the Indians make expeditions into the desert, each man having yoked together three camels—a female in the middle, with a male like a trace-horse to draw on each side. On the female he himself rides, having taken care that she be one taken for yoking from her young—the more recently born the better. For their female camels are not inferior to horses in speed, and they can carry much greater weights besides.
